title: Perpetua's ladder
hookLine: in a vision she climbs a narrow ladder, stepping on a dragon's head
tomorrow: you've done everything on the list. so what else is there?

lines: THE FIRST STAIR IN THE DARK.
cards: The first stair in a dark house has its own feel: the creak, the cold rail, the weight tipping forward. A young mother in prison, Perpetua, once saw a first step she never forgot.
Her brother had asked her to pray for a vision: would this end in suffering or in release? That night she saw a ladder reaching up to heaven, and lying underneath it, a dragon.
What do you do with a dragon under your ladder? She put her foot on its head.

teach.b: This comes from the Passion of Perpetua and Felicity, and these chapters are told in her own voice. Notice how much of it you can feel. First, the ladder.
It's so narrow only one person can climb at a time.
Second, the blades. Swords, spears, hooks and knives are fixed to its sides. Climb carelessly, or keep looking around, and you get torn.
Third, the step. Saturus, the man who taught them the faith, climbs first. At the top he turns: Perpetua, I'm waiting for you, but don't let the dragon bite you.
In the name of Jesus Christ, she answers, it won't hurt me.

teach.h: THE DRAGON BECOMES THE FIRST STEP.
teach.b: The dragon slowly lifts its head out from under the ladder, as if afraid of her, and she treads on it as her first step.
Some readers hear Genesis here, where the Douay-Rheims says of the woman and the serpent: "she shall crush thy head." Fourth, the taste.
At the top is a wide garden and a gray-haired man dressed as a shepherd, milking sheep, with people in white all around. He gives her a mouthful of cheese, and everyone says Amen.
She wakes still tasting something sweet, and she understands: it will be suffering.
She tells her brother, and the climb goes on.

how: Catholics name Perpetua and Felicity in the Roman Canon, the first Eucharistic Prayer, and keep their feast together each year.

o: a list of virtues she wrote for her young son
her vision of a narrow climb begun on a dragon's head
a rope ladder she used to escape from the prison

p: so narrow, only one at a time
climbs first and waits for her
a sweet taste still there on waking

s: Perpetua's story only survives in legends written about her
these chapters of the Passion are told in her own voice.
in the vision, the dragon lifts its head as if afraid of her
and she treads on it as her first step up.
the vision tells her she'll be released from prison
she wakes and understands that it will be suffering.

games.q: your friend wants to audition for a music program, but the whole thing terrifies her, so she keeps planning the entire year instead. what's Perpetua's move?
o: find the very first step, and take only that.
wait until the fear goes away on its own.
pick a safer program with no audition at all.
games.why: Perpetua didn't solve the ladder from the bottom. the thing that frightened her became her first step, taken in the name of Jesus Christ.

practice: Find a stair, a step, or even a curb, and stand at the bottom of it. Name one thing crouching under your plans, then lift your foot and set it down on the first step, slowly, feeling your weight move.
Stay there a few breaths before you come down.

wordCard.voice: Perpetua's ladder. A narrow climb lined with blades, and a dragon that turned out to be the first rung.

orig.note: Latin for dragon or great serpent: the creature lying under Perpetua's ladder.

carryVoice: Your line: step on the dragon. What frightened her became the way up. See you soon.
